title: Coding Problems
instructions:
Write your C# code in each box. Press Tab to indent.

You may use:
• Debug.Log, variables, and operators
• if / else if / else
• loops, arrays, and foreach
• methods (parameters, return values, overloads, optional parameters)
• classes (new and the dot operator)

Use clear names and no magic numbers.

questions.prompt:
COUNT THE ITEM   (5 pts)

Goal: Write a method that counts how many times an item shows up in an inventory array.

What to write:
   • A method named CountItem
   • It takes 2 parameters:
        – a string array named inventory
        – a string named itemName
   • It RETURNS how many slots in inventory exactly match itemName

Then:
   • Declare a string array
   • Call CountItem on it
   • Use Debug.Log to print the number it returns


Example 1
   inventory = { "torch", "rusty key", "torch", "rusty sword" }
   itemName  = "torch"
   Prints:   2
   (Two slots hold "torch".)

Example 2
   inventory = { "rusty key", "rusty sword" }
   itemName  = "torch"
   Prints:   0
   (No slot holds "torch".)

FIGHTER CLASS   (10 pts)

Goal: Build a Fighter class, then use two Fighter objects to run a hero-vs-goblin fight and print who wins.

Step 1: Write a class named Fighter
   Member variables (all public):
      • string name
      • int health
      • int attack

   Methods:
      • TakeDamage(int amount)
           Lowers health by amount.
           Health never goes below 0.
      • IsDefeated()
           Returns a bool: true when health is 0.
      • Attack(Fighter target)
           The target takes damage equal to this fighter's attack.

Step 2: In Start, create two fighters with new
      • a hero and a goblin
      • set each one's name, health, and attack

Step 3: Run the fight in rounds
      • The hero attacks first.
      • Then the goblin attacks, only if it is not defeated.
      • Repeat until one fighter is defeated.

Step 4: Print the winner
      • Use Debug.Log to print the winner's name, then the word wins
           (for example:  Hero wins)


Example 1
   Hero:     name "Hero",   health 100,   attack 6
   Goblin:   name "Goblin", health 30,    attack 8
   Prints:   Hero wins
   (The goblin reaches 0 on the hero's 5th attack. The hero still has 68 health.)

Example 2
   Hero:     name "Hero",   health 20,    attack 6
   Goblin:   name "Goblin", health 30,    attack 8
   Prints:   Goblin wins
   (After 3 rounds the hero has 0 health. The goblin still has 12.)
